claims.text: A reactive interatomic potential tailored to oxidation kinetics can accurately simulate oxidation of metallic surfaces.
Such simulations can inform the design of oxidation-resistant metallic surfaces.
Unprotected metallic systems are prone to oxidation under high-temperature or chemically reactive conditions.
High temperatures and abundant oxygen accelerate oxidation.
Embedding a reactive potential in an atomistic simulation enables detailed capture of oxygen-metal interactions.
Embedding a reactive potential in an atomistic simulation enables detailed capture of oxide-scale evolution.
The tailored reactive potential accurately models the formation and growth of protective oxide scales.
The potential models protective oxide-scale formation by simulating oxygen adsorption and reaction kinetics.
The modeled adsorption and reaction kinetics can predict how environmental conditions affect oxidation resistance.
The simulation outputs will align with experimental oxidation kinetics.
The simulations will identify conditions under which protective oxide scales form reliably.
Identifying conditions for reliable protective oxide-scale formation can enhance oxidation resistance.
Unprotected metallic systems exhibit rapid oxidation without mitigation.
The model may have limited applicability outside its calibration range.
The reactive potential may not transfer reliably across different metallic alloys.
The reactive potential may not capture all oxidation mechanisms under extreme or variable conditions.
